transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with right now?

I’m having a really hard time doing anything quietly or calmly, even when I’m supposed to be relaxing. I always feel like I have to be moving or talking, and it’s starting to cause problems at work and at home, so I’d like help figuring out how to get this under control.

When you’re trying to focus on something like reading or work, do you mainly find your mind constantly drifting to worries and ‘what if’ thoughts, or is it more that your attention jumps around and you can’t stay on one task even if you’re not especially worried or sad?

It’s more that my attention jumps around and I can’t stay on one thing, even if I’m not particularly worried or upset. I’ll start reading or working, and then my mind just skips to something else and I feel like I need to get up or do something different.
Have you had this kind of restlessness and trouble staying on one task since you were a child (for example in school), or is it something that only started in the last few months or years?

It’s been there since I was a kid—I remember getting in trouble in elementary school for not staying in my seat and rushing through work. It’s just kind of always been how I am, and it’s continued right up to now.
Besides feeling restless, do you also often lose things, forget appointments or tasks, or make careless mistakes because you miss details, even when you’re really trying to pay attention?
Yeah, that happens to me a lot. I’ll forget appointments unless I set multiple reminders, and I misplace things like my keys or work badge all the time even when I’m trying to be careful.
Do you also find yourself acting or speaking on impulse—like interrupting others, blurting things out, or making decisions quickly without thinking them through—and then regretting it afterward?

Yeah, I do that a lot—I interrupt people or blurt out what I’m thinking before they’re finished talking. I usually realize it right after and feel bad or embarrassed, especially if I’ve cut someone off in a meeting or said something too blunt.

Do these attention and restlessness problems cause significant difficulties for you in more than one area of life—for example at work or school, at home, and in relationships—not just in one specific situation?

Yeah, it affects me pretty much everywhere. At work I have trouble sitting through meetings and staying on one task, and at home I can’t seem to just relax—I’m always pacing or fidgeting, which annoys my partner. It also causes issues in conversations because I jump in or change topics and people get frustrated.

Have you ever been evaluated or treated before for attention or hyperactivity problems—like being diagnosed with ADHD or taking medication for it—or is this the first time you’re seeking help for these symptoms?

I’ve never had a formal evaluation for attention or hyperactivity before—this is the first time I’m really seeking help for it. No one’s ever officially diagnosed me with ADHD or put me on medication for it, though teachers and family have commented on me being “hyper” or unable to sit still since I was a kid.

When you’re really interested in something—like a hobby or a favorite show or game—are you able to focus on it for long periods, or do you still find your attention jumping around and needing to move or switch activities a lot?

If it’s something I really like, I can sometimes get into it for a bit, but I still end up fidgeting, getting up, or checking my phone and bouncing between things. Even with a favorite show or game, I’ll pause it, wander around, or switch to something else instead of just staying with it calmly.

Along with the restlessness and attention problems, do you also have long periods—at least two weeks—of feeling very down, hopeless, or extremely anxious most days, or are your mood and anxiety generally okay between the attention issues?

I don’t think I’ve had long stretches like two weeks straight of feeling really hopeless or severely anxious most days. I have ups and downs and get stressed, but overall my mood and anxiety feel mostly okay aside from being frustrated with how restless and scattered I am.

Because of your distractibility or acting on impulse, have you had any serious problems like car accidents, getting fired or written up at work, or major conflicts in relationships that you feel wouldn’t have happened otherwise?

Nothing really extreme like a serious car accident or getting fired. I’ve had a couple of close calls while driving because I got distracted by my phone or something outside, and I’ve gotten a warning at work for speaking out of turn in meetings, but nothing beyond that.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with right now?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong pattern, beginning in childhood, of marked hyperactivity, restlessness, impulsivity, and difficulty sustaining attention across multiple settings (school, work, home, relationships). Symptoms include inability to sit still, talking and moving excessively, interrupting others, and difficulty remaining on task even when not anxious or depressed. These symptoms cause clear functional impairment at work and at home, and there is no evidence of a primary mood or anxiety disorder driving the presentation. This is most consistent with Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive type (F90.0) under ICD-10.
